overloadPatches.semanticRole: Deletes every index (keyword or standard) built on the field referenced by fieldPtr, but leaves any composite index containing that field untouched.

discriminatedBy.rule: Same declared type (Pointer, Text) as overload 2's indexName; which one applies depends on whether the value/pointer designates a field or an index name, not on its static type.

overloadPatches.semanticRole: Deletes only the single, specifically named index (keyword, standard, or composite) referenced by indexName.

discriminatedBy.rule: Same declared type (Pointer, Text) as overload 1's fieldPtr; which one applies depends on whether the value/pointer designates a field or an index name, not on its static type.

constraints: Overloads 1 and 2 declare the identical parameter type (Pointer, Text). Which one applies depends on what the pointer/name actually references at runtime -- not checkable from the call site alone.
If there is no index corresponding to fieldPtr or indexName, the command does nothing.
The trailing optional '*' performs the deindexing asynchronously: the calling method continues execution immediately regardless of whether the index deletion has finished.
